NFL DFS Tight End Rankings: Week 11 (DraftKings)

DraftKings main slate · Sunday, November 22 · 10 games · By Chris Spags · · Numbers as of November 21, 10:25 AM ET

Trey McBride is the top-projected tight end on the Week 11 DraftKings main slate at 14.0 DraftKings points for $6,600, at Kansas City. Brock Bowers (13.4, $7,300) and Colston Loveland (13.3, $5,100) are next.

Colston Loveland returns the most per dollar among tight ends projected for at least 7 points: 2.61 projected points per $1,000 at $5,100.

Every projection is a SPAGS model estimate from the November 21, 10:25 AM ET run of the Splash Play NFL model. This page updates each time the main-slate numbers are published.

Tight ends to know in Week 11

Trey McBride, ARI at KC ($6,600)

Trey McBride carries the highest SPAGS model projection at the position, 14.0 DraftKings points at $6,600. That is 0.6 points clear of Brock Bowers. The model gives him 11.9 targets on 34.8 routes. The salary works out to 2.12 projected points per $1,000, 10th of 12 at the position. Across 10,000 simulations McBride averaged 14.1 points with a simulated floor of 2.5 and a ceiling of 38.5, and he holds 5% of the simulated winning-lineup credit. Arizona is a 16.5-point underdog on the road against Kansas City, with an implied team total of 12 in a game totaled at 40.5.

Brock Bowers, LV at DEN ($7,300)

Brock Bowers projects 2nd at the position with 13.4 DraftKings points at $7,300. The model gives him 7.8 targets on 30.9 routes. The salary works out to 1.84 projected points per $1,000, 11th of 12 at the position. Across 10,000 simulations Bowers averaged 13.5 points with a simulated floor of 1.9 and a ceiling of 37.6, and he holds 2% of the simulated winning-lineup credit. Las Vegas is a 10.5-point underdog on the road against Denver, with an implied team total of 15 in a game totaled at 40.5.

Value: Mark Andrews, BAL at CAR ($3,500)

Mark Andrews projects for 9.1 DraftKings points at $3,500, which works out to 2.60 points per $1,000 of salary. That is the best rate of any player priced in the cheaper half of the 12 tight ends the model projects for 7 or more points. The model gives him 4.8 targets on 20.2 routes. Across 10,000 simulations Andrews averaged 9.0 points with a simulated floor of 0.0 and a ceiling of 30.2, and he holds 11% of the simulated winning-lineup credit. Baltimore is a 3-point underdog on the road against Carolina, with an implied team total of 20.25 in a game totaled at 43.5.
